_comment_mesh: Local-first mesh endpoint + stable MagicDNS names. Leave endpoint empty to DEFAULT to the pki node's primary LAN IPv4 (http://<lanip>:8080) so the node works before any public DNS exists. Set endpoint (or .headscale.server_url, or the brand HEADSCALE_URL) to a public facade ONLY once it is published. cp_dns_name is the STABLE control-plane name used as kubeadm controlPlaneEndpoint + every join target; magic_dns_domain is headscale dns.base_domain.
_comment_tailscale_ssh: HARDENED: Tailscale SSH (--ssh in up_args) is on by default and the headscale SSH ACL (policy.hujson) restricts SSH sessions to ssh_user ONLY (root + others denied). ssh_user is the image's PRIVILEGED user — the SUPERADMIN/admin in users.json; leave empty to default to the first sudo user. The operator SSHs in over the tailnet with the keys-out/ssh/<admin>_ed25519 PRIVATE key (off-image, key-USB custody); its public key is baked into that user's authorized_keys. Set tailscale.ssh=false to opt a node out.
_comment_kubernetes: FIRST control-plane: role=control-plane + bootstrap=true (+ first defaults true) -> kubeadm init --upload-certs. ADDITIONAL control-plane: role=control-plane, bootstrap=true, first=false, and a full join block incl. certificate_key -> kubeadm join --control-plane. Workers: role=worker + a join block. Leave join.api_server empty to auto-target the stable cp_dns_name:6443. ETCD SECRET ENCRYPTION-AT-REST: keys-provision writes /etc/kubernetes/encryption-config.yaml (aescbc) before kubeadm init so the apiserver encrypts Secrets in etcd. Put the shared key at kubernetes/encryption-key on THIS stick (base64 32 bytes; same file on every control plane) so all apiservers decrypt the same etcd — else a fresh key is minted on the first CP and must be copied by hand. NEVER in git.
_comment_update: OPT-IN (default-off) host-binary auto-update. This whole block is OPTIONAL: omit it and the node stays OFF (absence => OFF, fail-safe-to-off). Present only to pre-seed an opt-in / tune cadence at provision time; the live devops/snapdragon-update-policy ConfigMap (superadmin UI) overrides these at runtime. enabled:true opts in / enables (default false); cadence is the cron the node runs; window (HH:MM-HH:MM, local) gates the pull live; reboot=if-needed|never|always (kured-safe); staging maps a board/role/'client' key to a cadence for staged waves.
_comment_vault: Vault is PERSISTENT + AUTO-UNSEALING (manifests/vault: Raft on the LUKS /mnt/data, TLS listener, Shamir seal). Custody (NEVER git, same offline USB model as the cluster CA + luks.key): vault/token = the bootstrap/root token (seeds the vault-bootstrap Secret the vault-pki-init Job authenticates with, and the external-secrets vault-token Secret for ESO); vault/unseal-key = the Shamir unseal key (seeds the vault-unseal Secret the auto-unseal sidecar uses to unseal on every restart). Produce both ONCE with `vault operator init -key-shares=1 -key-threshold=1` after first deploy, write them to the KEYS stick, and keep them offline. See keys-template/vault/README.md + docs/ENCRYPTION-AT-REST.md.
_comment_mail: OPTIONAL outbound mail (SMTP) — ABSENT BY DEFAULT. This block only DOCUMENTS the mail creds the KEYS USB carries (in secrets/mail.json, mirrored into vault/secrets.json as the casdoor-smtp/akkoma-smtp Secrets). With enabled:false (or empty user/password) NO SMTP is wired: Casdoor + Akkoma keep native login + admin-approval registration. 'provider' (protonmail default | gmail | outlook | smtp | none) selects the host/port/tls preset; secrets/mail.json holds the actual user/password/from/dkim. Generated by scripts/gen-provision-keys.sh; seeded to Vault secret/<brand>/mail by scripts/gen-cluster-secrets.sh.
_comment_storage: Attached data disk(s) that back the cluster PVCs (/mnt/data via the snapdragon-local StorageClass) + relocated containerd/kubelet/Vault state. ENCRYPTION AT REST (LUKS2, aes-xts-plain64, argon2id) is ON by default per device (encrypt:true); set a device's encrypt:false only to opt out. Key custody (NEVER in git): luks_keyfile points at a keyfile on THIS KEYS stick (default secrets/luks.key) — the Pi5-without-TPM unlock slot; luks_tpm2:true additionally enrolls TPM2 auto-unlock (systemd-cryptenroll/clevis) on x86 / TPM-equipped nodes so they boot without the USB, with the keyfile as recovery. format:true is REQUIRED to luksFormat a blank disk (destroys data); an already-LUKS disk is just reopened. See docs/ENCRYPTION-AT-REST.md.
